standard_prerequisites.name: Vanishing of higher cohomology of abelian sheaves on a Noetherian space of dimension at most one
standard_prerequisites.use: Kills H^2 and hence the obstruction to lifting unit classes.

standard_prerequisites.name: Cohomology of a closed immersion and the Picard group as H^1 of the unit sheaf
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Stacks Project, Cohomology, Lemma cohomology-lemma-cohomology-and-closed-immersions (tag 02UV) and Lemma cohomology-lemma-h1-invertible (tag 09NU)
standard_prerequisites.use: Translate the two H^1 groups into groups of invertible sheaves on Z and X.

core_obligations: Write the short exact sequence 0 -> (1+I) cap O_X^* -> O_X^* -> i_*O_Z^* -> 0 of sheaves of abelian groups on X, where I is the ideal sheaf of Z (proof lines 8145-8151).
Use dim(X) <= 1 to conclude H^2(X, F) = 0 for every abelian sheaf F, hence surjectivity of H^1(X, O_X^*) -> H^1(X, i_*O_Z^*) (proof lines 8152-8155).
Identify H^1(X, i_*O_Z^*) with H^1(Z, O_Z^*) via the closed-immersion comparison and conclude using the identification of the Picard group with H^1 of the unit sheaf (proof lines 8156-8160).
proof_roadmap: Produce the unit-sheaf exact sequence attached to the closed immersion.
Use the dimension bound to kill the obstruction in H^2.
Move to Z and reinterpret in terms of Picard groups.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves surjectivity of Pic(X) -> Pic(Z) for a closed immersion i : Z -> X whose target has Noetherian underlying space of dimension at most one. The proof writes the short exact sequence of sheaves of abelian groups 0 -> (1+I) cap O_X^* -> O_X^* -> i_*O_Z^* -> 0 associated to the ideal sheaf I of Z, observes that H^2(X, F) = 0 for every abelian sheaf F because dim(X) <= 1, and deduces surjectivity of H^1(X, O_X^*) -> H^1(X, i_*O_Z^*) (proof lines 8145-8155). The identification H^1(X, i_*O_Z^*) = H^1(Z, O_Z^*) and the interpretation of H^1 of the unit sheaf as the Picard group then give the statement (proof lines 8156-8160). H2: the exact sequence together with the dimension-two vanishing is the substance.
